verdict.rationale: Gazebo's plugin architecture lets you build custom robot, sensor and environment control plugins, and gz-transport message passing decouples external application code from the simulator. ros_gz also implies ROS-based apps can talk to simulated hardware. The only explicit swappable abstraction in the evidence, though, is the plugin interface to physics engines (ODE, Bullet, DART), not sensors or actuators. Missing for 10: documented stable hardware-abstraction interfaces for sensors/actuators, evidence that swapping sensors or actuators (or sim vs. real hardware) requires no application-code changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
